text.p: Judith Wiesner, Austria's most successful women's tennis player and the world number 17, said on Monday she will retire at the end of the year.

Wiesner, 31, has been sidelined by a virus illness since the middle of March. She has won a total of $1.7 million during her 12-year professional career and was a quarter-finalist at Wimbledon and U.S. Open last year.
"I had a long time to think while I was ill and I just couldn't find sufficient motivation for 1998," she said. "Ever since taking this decision, I am able to look forward to my next tournaments."
Wiesner, whose highest world ranking was 12th, still has tournaments in Berlin, Strassbourg and Paris on her schedule as well as Wimbledon and the U.S. Open.
She will also play for Austria in the Fed Cup in July.
